messages:
Alicia (eng-runtime): quick heads-up — noticed non-deterministic token deltas when we replay production traces with the new kernel selector + anonymized prefix-rewrite mode :eyes:
Ben (eng-ml): details? kernel selector as in runtime switching to quantized kernels during step 1?
Alicia (eng-runtime): yeah. test flow: take scrubbed trace slice, run harness with --anon=prefix-rewrite (stable hashing) and compare output logits. When runtime chooses trt-int8 vs trt-fp16 we see ~0.6% token divergence after token 32 rather than tiny float noise
Casey (eng-sre): are we sure this is replay harness determinism and not network/ordering? how are you running the harness?
Alicia (eng-runtime): running local harness binary on identical VM image, pinned seed, no network. command: `./trace_playback --trace traces/slice-2026-02.json --anon=prefix-rewrite --seed=1337 --batch-profile=prod-small --kernel-preference=auto`
Alicia (eng-runtime): also tried forcing `--kernel=trt-int8` vs `--kernel=trt-fp16` and the divergence persists — seems kernel choice changes KV warm-up contents (different kv eviction/stride) which shifts subsequent attention windows
Ben (eng-ml): hmm kv cache layout differences across kernels could change numeric accumulation (different blocking). parity debug idea: run single-request deterministic harness that snapshots KV state after each layer and compare diffs layer-by-layer
Dana (privacy): reminder — prefix-rewrite anonymization rewrites user prefixes with stable tokens (hash->tokenN) to keep semantics while anonymizing. we must preserve determinism across runs for audits. any workaround that weakens anonymization is not acceptable
Alicia (eng-runtime): agreed. initial hypothesis: prefix-rewrite sometimes changes input tokenization length (rare unicode combos) which makes warm-up batches different. even if mapping is stable, token length changes lead to different batching boundaries -> different kernel path chosen at runtime
Casey (eng-sre): practical repro plan: 1) deterministic 1k-sample microtrace where we record tokenized lengths before/after anon rewrite 2) run harness with `--batching-mode=static` vs `--batching-mode=adaptive` 3) compare p95/p99 latencies and token parity hashes
Ben (eng-ml): I'll add a small parity tool: `parity-check --snapshot-kv --snapshot-layer=all --write-diff` to highlight first layer where diverge appears. put outputs in /tmp/parity-2287654321/
Alicia (eng-runtime): ran quick parity-check forcing static batching and fixed kernel (trt-fp16) — parity held across runs. switching kernel selector->auto breaks parity at layer 3 consistently.
Dana (privacy): does static batching + stable kernel selector violate our apples-to-apples goal for perf comparisons? if we lock kernel we might hide selector regressions. we need both: apples-to-apples baseline and selector-on tests
Casey (eng-sre): propose two-phase load test: A) apples-to-apples baseline: fixed kernel, static batching, KV warmup enabled, run 10k requests (ramp 0->200 rps) report token-level parity rate + perf metrics. B) selector-on stress: same trace + same seed but allow auto kernel selection and adaptive batching to measure divergence frequency and perf benefits. compare delta in p95 and token-parity.
Ben (eng-ml): agree. metrics to collect: token_parity_rate (pct identical tokens), first_layer_divergence_layer (int), p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, kernel_map (counts of requests served by each kernel), kv_warmup_hit_rate.
Alicia (eng-runtime): action items: 1) I'll add token-length snapshot before/after anon rewrite into harness logs (quick patch) 2) Ben adds layer snapshot diffs + a compact parity summary 3) Casey will run two-phase load test on our perf pool (g6-48) next Tue morning 4) Dana to review anon logs to ensure no PII slips in snapshots
Dana (privacy): note — snapshots must be hashed and truncated, no raw text. acceptable format: `sha256(tokenized_prefix) -> token_len` and layer-kv fingerprints only (not raw kv values).
Casey (eng-sre): planning slack to perf-run channel with schedule and expected resource usage. I'll spin up dedicated pool with identical GPU firmware to avoid driver-induced kernel variability
Alicia (eng-runtime): small repro snippet I used for parity: ```
# reproducible run
./trace_playback --trace traces/sample-100.json --anon=prefix-rewrite --anon-hash-seed=1337 \
  --seed=1337 --batching-mode=static --kernel=trt-fp16 --snapshot-prefix-lens=/tmp/prefix_lens.json \
  --snapshot-kv=/tmp/kv_snap1 --layers=all
```
Ben (eng-ml): I'll wire parity-check to output a short report like: `PARITY_OK=bool, FIRST_DIFF_LAYER=3, TOKENS_IDENTICAL=998/1000` and attach per-kernel stats.
Alicia (eng-runtime): note for future: consider making kernel selection deterministic for replay runs by seeding kernel policy with request fingerprint so we can do apples-to-apples across kernels automatically
Dana (privacy): fine as long as fingerprinting uses hashed metadata only (no user content).
Casey (eng-sre): ok team — I'll run the baseline A on Tue 09:00 PT, then B at 12:00 PT. expect ~3 hours each. will post results + artifacts. :thumbsup:
replay-bot: scheduled job `parity-loadtest-2287654321` created, status: queued
Alicia (eng-runtime): thanks — will follow up with layer diffs and a short summary once Ben's tool runs.
Ben (eng-ml): thumbs up, will push parity-check by EOD and add small CI check for future kernel merges (quick smoke).
Dana (privacy): I'll review artifacts after tests and sign off if redaction rules hold.
Casey (eng-sre): closing loop: if parity failures > 0.5% we treat as a regression and roll back selector heuristics for the affected kernel configs.
Alicia (eng-runtime): noted. thanks everyone — feel free to DM if you need logs earlier.
